newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-STV sees improved ad sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-STV sees improved ad sales.

text.p: Scottish Television Plc plans to boost its advertising sales by offering deals extending to its newly acquired newspaper titles, executive chairman Gus Macdonald said on Tuesday.
"We are developing bi-media deals for advertising to drive the bottom line of both sides of the business," Macdonald told Reuters in an interview.

STV, the commercial television (ITV) company for central Scotland, completed the acquisition of Glasgow-based Caledonian Publishing for 120 million pounds last October. Caledonian publishes The Herald and the Evening Times.
The Herald is the leading quality broadsheet in central Scotland while the Evening Times is an evening tabloid sold in the Glasgow area.
STV posted record 1996 profits of 61.2 million pounds, boosted by exceptional gains of 33.2 million, the bulk of which came from the sale of its stakes in HTV and ITN to United News & Media.
Pre-tax profit excluding exceptionals rose 40 percent to 28 million pounds.
Macdonald said STV's eight percent advertising revenue growth was the highest in the ITV network. Ad revenue climbed to 81.4 million pounds, a market share of 4.9 percent.
He added that there was no apparent impact on sales from the impending launch of Channel 5, the new UK commercial terrestrial channel which goes on air on March 30.
Competition from Channel 5 should be limited as it will not be possible to pick up its signal in large areas of Glasgow.
STV, in which Mirror Group Plc and Flextech Plc each have 20 percent stakes, said its main task for 1997 was integrating Caledonian.
Macdonald said the company was well on the way to achieving planned three million pound cost savings. The acquisition boosts its workforce from 600 to 1,400.
